:::{#def-determinant}
#### Determinant

The **determinant** of a $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$
with entries $a_{ij}$,
written $\det(\matr{A})$ or $\abs{\matr{A}}$,
is the number defined recursively in $p$:

- For $p = 1$, $\det(\matr{A}) = a_{11}$.
- For $p \ge 2$,
  $$
  \det(\matr{A}) = \sum_{j=1}^p (-1)^{1+j}\, a_{1j} \det\paren{\matr{A}_{(1j)}},
  $$
  where $\matr{A}_{(1j)}$ is the $(p-1) \times (p-1)$ matrix
  left after deleting row $1$ and column $j$ of $\matr{A}$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This recursive formula is the *cofactor expansion* along the first row.
Other sources define the determinant
as a sum over all orderings of the columns
and derive this expansion from it;
the two definitions agree
[@banerjee2014linear; see also <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant>].

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-determinant}
#### Determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix

For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$,
deleting row 1 and column 1 leaves $\begin{bmatrix} d \end{bmatrix}$,
and deleting row 1 and column 2 leaves $\begin{bmatrix} c \end{bmatrix}$.
So:

$$
\ba
\det(\matr{A})
&= (-1)^{1+1}\, a \det\paren{\begin{bmatrix} d \end{bmatrix}}
 + (-1)^{1+2}\, b \det\paren{\begin{bmatrix} c \end{bmatrix}}
&& \text{(definition, } p = 2 \text{)}
\\
&= a d - b c
&& \text{(definition, } p = 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

For example,
$\det\paren{\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}} = 2 \cd 2 - 1 \cd 1 = 3$.

:::
